findings.body: A ready item causes this call to enter `nextstep._item`, which calls `repo.merge_setting` (src/forge/nextstep.py:550–552). That fetches the default branch from origin (src/forge/repo.py:171–178). When GitHub is unreachable, the fetch raises and the entire board command fails instead of returning retained rows with unknown checks. Merged items with retained worktrees take the same path at nextstep.py:532–533. Keep the view available when this permission lookup fails, using a null next command if necessary. The current offline test fails only the gh request while leaving its local Git remote reachable.
findings.title: Not done: GitHub-unreachable board rows with unknown checks

findings.body: After a successful `forge close`, the saved status remains `waiting for checks` (src/forge/close.py:174–179); readiness is written to the shared ready receipt at close.py:214–218. The next-step code recognizes that receipt and derives `ready` (src/forge/nextstep.py:538–543), but this field returns the unchanged saved status. Consequently, both task children and fix rows continue reporting the checks-waiting stage even while their next command is `forge merge`. Derive the exposed stage from the same validated readiness evidence. The lifecycle test currently goes directly from close to merge without checking this intermediate board state.
findings.title: Not done: report ready tasks and fixes at their current stage

findings.body: GitHub supports the terminal conclusion `STALE` ([CheckConclusionState](https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/reference/checks#checkconclusionstate)), but this failure list omits it. A completed stale check therefore becomes `unknown` and produces no failure occurrence, although Forge's existing gate classifies it as red (src/forge/checks.py:68–70). Include this supported unsuccessful conclusion so the board and occurrence stream agree with the merge gate.
findings.title: Classify stale completed checks as failed
